choices.text: More than 1/2, because tails is due after the run of heads
Exactly 1/2, because the tosses are independent
Less than 1/2, because heads is on a streak

questions.feedback: That due feeling is the trap: After five heads in a row, tails is due. Reteach point: The coin never remembers: after five heads the next toss is still 1/2.
questions.misconception: After five heads in a row, tails is due.
questions.prompt: A fair coin has landed heads five times in a row. What is the probability of tails on the next toss?

questions.feedback: Two checks in one: probabilities must sum to 1, and expectation weights values by probabilities. If you averaged 0, 1, 2 equally you treated the outcomes as equally likely - the probabilities 0.2, 0.5, 0.3 say they are not.
questions.prompt: For X with probabilities 0.2, 0.5, 0.3 at values 0, 1, 2, verify the table is a valid distribution and compute E(X).

questions.feedback: Both halves are needed: choose which 3 trials succeed (10 choose 3 = 120 ways), then the path probability (0.3)^3(0.7)^7. Dropping the coefficient is the classic binomial slip.
questions.prompt: For a binomial distribution with n = 10 and p = 0.3, which expression gives P(X = 3)?

questions.answer: Between 90 and 110: one standard deviation each side of the mean, 100 - 10 and 100 + 10.
questions.feedback: The 68-95-99.7 rule: about 68% within one standard deviation of the mean, about 95% within two, about 99.7% within three. Anchor on the mean first, then step out in standard deviations.
questions.prompt: A normal distribution has mean 100 and standard deviation 10. Between which two values does about 68% of the distribution lie?
